raw_response:
The silver step sets txn_date to CAST(ingest_ts AS DATE). That was probably introduced in the DE-398 refactor on 2026-01-16. Ingest_ts is the delivery time, 02:00 on the day after the transaction, so txn_date is off by one day. The alert counts 4558 rows, which equals every POSTED row, so all of them are affected.

The correct derivation is CAST(txn_ts AS DATE), and the alert itself says txn_date should match the date of txn_ts. The sample rows show txn_ts falling on the day before ingest_ts, so the batch delivery pattern is consistent with this.

Possible complications: late-arriving data, or transactions whose txn_ts date differs from the batch date. Batch 1 has ingest_ts of 01-06 and txn_ts min is 01-05, so this is consistent with a one-day lag. Using txn_ts is unambiguous.

The fix replaces silver_transactions, and the gold tables follow from it. Nothing else looks problematic: there are no duplicate txn_ids (distinct = rows), and all customers and merchants appear to be covered. The status filter is kept as-is.

Deriving txn_date from txn_ts fixes silver and the downstream gold tables.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.93, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(txn_ts AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
